title: Elasticsearch cluster outage — native OOM on Lucene mmap, no master, all writes failed (2026-04-13)
diagnosis: Two of three Elasticsearch cluster nodes crashed due to native (OS-level) out-of-memory errors on Lucene mmap segment file allocation, not JVM heap OOM. Each node has 30 GB RAM with no swap; JVM is configured with 16 GB heap + 8 GB direct memory, leaving only ~6 GB for OS+kernel+Lucene mmap segments. During elevated background merge activity, the remaining native memory was exhausted on two nodes within 21 hours, causing mmap ENOMEM and process death. Node 3 (prod-elasticsearch-audittrail-03) crashed first on 2026-04-12 09:31 UTC and went undetected because there was no port-level monitoring. When Node 2 also crashed on 2026-04-13 06:49 UTC, the cluster lost quorum and went read-only. Both nodes had Restart=no in their systemd units so they did not auto-recover. RabbitMQ accumulated failed-event writes with 'cluster_block_exception: no master'. Manual restart at ~12:23 UTC restored the cluster; no data lost. Mitigations already applied (per PIR): Restart=on-failure enabled on all three nodes, Centreon ES port 9200 TCP check added, cluster-health-status check added. Still pending: reduce JVM heap to 12 GB and remove/reduce MaxDirectMemorySize, add 2-4 GB emergency swap with vm.swappiness=1, reduce shard count from 14,248 toward <3,000 via ILM.
playbook: 1) On 'ES writes failing' / 'cluster_block_exception: no master' alerts, immediately check all three ES nodes via the new Centreon port-9200 check; if any port-9200 fail, that node is dead. 2) Confirm cluster health endpoint — RED means master lost. 3) Mitigation: SSH to the dead node(s), confirm the elasticsearch process is gone, restart manually (systemctl restart elasticsearch) — Restart=on-failure should now auto-restart but verify. 4) Confirm RabbitMQ ES-audit queue is draining once cluster is back. 5) Cross-check whether the still-pending mitigations (heap reduction, swap, shard reduction) have shipped — if not, escalate.

title: Race condition nullifying ServerTimeModified causes some Method saves to skip syncing to QuickBooks / Xero
diagnosis: Newly introduced code that resets Xero's ServerTimeModified back to null after a successful sync inadvertently affected the QB path too, sometimes nullifying ServerTimeModified BEFORE the actual sync had run. This was a race condition (intermittent), so records would silently fail to enqueue to QB. Mitigated by rolling back the offending code. Follow-up migration in progress to identify and re-set ServerTimeModified for the records that were missed and push them to QB.
playbook: 1) If customers report 'some saves not appearing in QB/Xero' shortly after a Method release, check the most recent commits touching ServerTimeModified handling (Xero sync code). 2) Confirm intermittent (not full outage) by sampling sync logs for the affected accounts. 3) Mitigation: roll back the offending change. 4) Recovery: run a migration to set ServerTimeModified back on the missed records and push them through.

title: Method-wide outage during morning release when ms-preferences-api shipped [AllowInternal]/[AllowIdentity] tags before dependent services updated (PL-62401)
diagnosis: While hardening weak external security checks on ms-preferences-api, the team added [AllowInternal]/[AllowIdentity] tags so external callers would be blocked and upstream services would route through the internal routes instead. Nine services depend on ms-preferences-api. ms-preferences-api was released first; the dependent services were still mid-release, so their existing calls to the public routes were now rejected, and Method was effectively down for all customers (sign-in errors plus loading-screen errors) until the morning releases were rolled back.
playbook: 1) If sign-in fails / loading screen breaks across the platform during a morning release window and ms-preferences-api is in the release set, check whether [AllowInternal]/[AllowIdentity] tags were just added without corresponding upstream caller updates. 2) Mitigation: roll back ms-preferences-api (or whichever security-hardened service shipped first). 3) Long-term per PIR: any release touching dependency-heavy security tags must be DevOps+Lead reviewed and scheduled outside business hours.

match.precedence_note: 2026-06-10: When ki-21 and ki-24 (ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring) both fire in the same 60-min window with ≥2 alerts each, treat as shared-upstream signal — investigate microservices.methodlocal.int pool state, runtime-core RTC backpressure, and ms-account-api / ms-preferences-api ClusterInfo lookup health together before classifying either independently. Repeated cross-channel co-firing (observed 3+ cycles per day this week) hardens the shared-upstream hypothesis; treating each as independent leads to wrong root-cause attribution.

diagnosis:
Frontend XHR errors (status_code:0, 'Failed to load') reported to DataDog RUM by method-ui are symptoms â€” the actual failure happens upstream in ms-gateway-api's Ocelot ResponderMiddleware, which raises RequestTimedOutError / TaskCanceledException while waiting for microservices.methodlocal.int (the .NET Framework Tier-3 IIS pool) to respond. Affected paths span multiple owned services on that pool: /syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync, /preferences/v3/User, /account/learning/progress, /account/banners/queue. The pattern is chronic â€” Ocelot warning volume in the 17:00 UTC hour was 1072 today vs 1064 24h ago (+0.7%), so the underlying timeout rate is steady-state, not a regression. DataDog monitor 77419271 ('Unusual number of XHR errors for account: {{@account_name.name}}') trips whenever a single account's user session bunches >40 such XHR errors within 5 min. NOTE: this *may* be downstream of ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota â€” DNS resolution failures on the Windows fleet manifest as Ocelot timeouts. Cross-reference both before concluding root cause.

2026-06-04 12:50Z surge (100x chronic baseline) traced to ms-account-api release at 12:30Z. Issue started 20 min post-deploy. Initial rollback of preferences + 'everything released today' did NOT resolve; targeted ms-account revert initiated 14:03Z. Runtime made 90K calls to ms-preferences-api in 30 min during surge -> 502 bad gateway. Lesson: when ki-21 shape fires at >10x chronic magnitude, always check ms-account / ms-preferences-api deploys explicitly (both currently absent from routines/triage.yaml repos:).
playbook: 1) Confirm chronic baseline by comparing ES Ocelot.Responder.Middleware Warning volume in the alert window vs the same window 24h ago â€” if delta < 20%, it's the chronic pattern (no new incident). 2) Aggregate timeouts by RequestPath: if dominant paths are all under upstream microservices.methodlocal.int, it's pool-level. 3) **Check ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota first** â€” DNS bursts on the Windows fleet present here as Ocelot timeouts. 4) If DNS is clean: identify which downstream microservice owns the slow path via Ocelot config in ms-gateway-api/gateway/API/ocelot.*.json. 5) Decision tree for the fix: (a) raise per-route Ocelot timeout (cheapest, masks symptom â€” appropriate if Ben prefers user-facing reliability over visibility), (b) scale microservices IIS pool / shorten recycle interval (medium cost, addresses cold-start tail), (c) profile the upstream microservice (sync-util / preferences / account) under prod load to find the slow path â€” root-cause fix but expensive.

DD APM trace search (not yet wired into dd_search.py) would pinpoint the slow span.

diagnosis: Client-side error from the Method native mobile app (iOS, observed UA Method/2.1.537 CFNetwork/Darwin). The app's one-time AsyncStorage->SecureStore storage migration fails with the iOS keychain error code ERR_KEY_CHAIN, logged server-side via mobilenative.method.me POST /apps/v1/logging/mobile (MethodUI.Controllers.LoggingController relay; dd_service 'nonprod/apps' on PROD-NEW-04/5/6 - ingestion hosts only, not a server fault). playbook: 1) Confirm volume + app version in ES: level:(ERROR OR FATAL) AND fields.dd_service:"nonprod/apps" AND message:"Failed to migrate from AsyncStorage" -- check fields.UserAgent for app version (e.g. Method/2.1.537) and OS (CFNetwork/Darwin = iOS). 2) This is a CLIENT bug: route to the mobile team. title: sp_UpdateCustomerItemPurchaseHistory fails with CREATE UNIQUE INDEX duplicate key (#PriceAdjusted IX_PA) for AppRoutine.Agent nightly job
diagnosis: Stored procedure sp_UpdateCustomerItemPurchaseHistory on tenant DBs (observed on cluster METHODDBCLUS1) fails with SqlException 1505: "The CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statement terminated because a duplicate key was found for the object name dbo.#PriceAdjusted_..._000001060FFF and the index name IX_PA. The duplicate key value is (435, 317, 1)." The SP populates a temp table #PriceAdjusted then attempts to create a UNIQUE INDEX IX_PA; duplicate rows in the temp data (same 3-column key (435, 317, 1) reproduces across many tenants) abort the index creation, leaving the nightly purchase-history refresh failed for that account. C# caller Runtime.Core.AppRoutine.Services.Application.Jobs.UpdatePurchaseHistoryJob.UpdatePurchaseHistoryForAccountAsync (line 238 of UpdatePurchaseHistoryJob.cs) is a thin Dapper wrapper that only invokes the SP -- the C# is unchanged since 2026-05-13 per git log. The SP itself was almost certainly migrated/patched on 2026-06-01 around 07:00-08:00Z (first ES hit at 07:48Z). 0 ES hits in the 6 days prior. Currently running 16-17 fires/day across 27+ distinct accounts on both AppRoutine.Agent VMs (ip-172-31-178-173 and ip-172-31-194-83). No user-visible outage; affected accounts get stale purchase-history data until fixed.
playbook: 1) Confirm the issue is current: ES query `level:Error AND "Purchase History Account - Processing Failed"` over the last 24h. Zero hits = resolved. 2) Pull the SP definition on METHODDBCLUS1: SSH to a SQL host and run `EXEC sp_helptext sp_UpdateCustomerItemPurchaseHistory` against any tenant DB; diff against the prior version (the SP is deployed through the Method.Data migration package). 3) Most likely fixes inside the SP: (a) add DISTINCT / GROUP BY to the INSERT INTO #PriceAdjusted SELECT statement, or (b) add WITH (IGNORE_DUP_KEY=ON) to the IX_PA index definition (silent dedupe -- safe iff duplicates are semantically equivalent). 4) Roll the fix to all tenant DBs via the same migration channel that introduced the regression. 5) Verify by re-running the nightly job for one previously-failed account (e.g. tfriedl, ppcindustries1) and confirming a successful row-count return from UpdatePurchaseHistoryJob.UpdatePurchaseHistoryForAccountAsync.

title: NullReferenceException in runtime-core UpdateViewsCommand when an IsLinked field has null LinkedViaTableName (reaches NormalizeViewName via RetrieveLinkedFieldsAsync) — PL-59777

any_of.regex: object reference.*not set.*instance of an object

diagnosis: Server-side NullReferenceException ('object reference not set') surfaced via Datadog error-tracking (monitor 227951254 'New issue to review', bot B063S8NBW0M) in #alert-runtime-monitoring. Root cause as identified and accepted by the runtime team (Richard Pangborn / Mohammad Syed Raihaan) in-channel on 2026-06-15: a field with IsLinked=true but a null LinkedViaTableName flows through RetrieveLinkedFieldsAsync into NormalizeViewName(), which is not null-safe, throwing the NRE. Two independent AI code-path analyses (Claude + Codex) converged on the same hypothesis. The defensive fix lives in runtime-core UpdateViewsCommand.cs (NOT ms-tables-fields-api, which a prior triage cycle initially guessed from symbol resolution on a 7-week-stale clone): guard the IsLinked/null-LinkedViaTableName case and/or make NormalizeViewName() null-safe. First observed for johnsandy's account in Work Orders (WO); the bad metadata state predates the crash and the team still needs to determine how the invalid data arose. NOTE: still unverified by reproduction as of KB creation (operator-accepted working hypothesis + PR in flight), so confidence is capped accordingly. Distinct from ki-2026-05-29-methodsession-getaccountbysubdomain-nre (a different NRE path: GetAccountBySubdomain / MethodSessionService.cs).
playbook: 1) Confirm the signature is the view/field-metadata NRE (NormalizeViewName / RetrieveLinkedFieldsAsync / null LinkedViaTableName), not the GetAccountBySubdomain NRE (ki-29). 2) Check PL-59777 status / whether the runtime-core UpdateViewsCommand.cs null-guard PR has merged + deployed. 3) If recurring post-deploy, the guard did not cover the path -- reopen with the fresh stack from logstash. 4) Identify the affected account (first seen: johnsandy/WO) and inspect its view/field metadata for IsLinked=true rows with null LinkedViaTableName to find/repair the source bad-data state. 5) ES/logstash is the only source of the .NET stack trace; if ES auth is down (chronic 401), rely on the operator thread + DD error-tracking issue id.

title: MIURL short-link domain unreachable — customers get browser "The site can't be reached" on Method short links (free-hour emails, portal links)
diagnosis: Customers receive the browser-level "This site can't be reached" page (a connection/DNS failure, not an in-app error) when following Method short links (MIURLs, generated by legacy-miurl-api — IIS app miurl.methodlocal.com, short URLs of form miurl.com/{hash}mI). Surfaced 2026-06-16 19:22Z via #swat: 4 customer reports relayed by Inder Dhaliwal, one via a 'free hour' customer email link, named account ebamethod (Bhumeek). Manan Kukreti reported the same symptom on #help-support the prior day (2026-06-15). Root cause is the active MIURL short-link DOMAIN being switched off miurl.cc to an alternate that is not resolving/serving; engineers (Arash Pakbaz, John Miranda, Richard Pangborn) reached consensus at ~19:42-19:50Z to revert the domain back to miurl.cc. No server-side telemetry available: legacy-miurl-api is .NET Framework and not Datadog-instrumented (DD 'miurl' query returned 0 results), and ES is chronically 401. Co-occurring sign-in synthetic monitor 127198928 was in Alert (>20s) but is a latency signal on a non-MIURL path — likely independent.
playbook: 1) On #swat/#help-support reports of customers getting browser 'site can't be reached' / 'can't be reached' when clicking Method short links (free-hour emails, portal links, MIURLs): suspect the MIURL short-link domain, NOT an app/server fault. 2) Confirm it's connection-level (browser error page), not an in-app XHR error — the request never reaches a Method server, so DD/ES will show nothing for the MIURL service. 3) Check what domain the short links currently resolve to vs miurl.cc; a recent short-link domain change is the prime suspect. 4) Mitigation: revert the MIURL short-link domain back to miurl.cc (the known-good domain) — confirmed effective by the team on 2026-06-16. 5) Long-term: add an external HTTP synthetic against the live MIURL domain (none exists today — the only signal was human reports), and keep miurl.cc as a permanent fallback. 6) Note legacy-miurl-api gotcha: changing HashIds salt/alphabet (HashIdsSetting) also breaks all existing short URLs — rule that out if the domain is reachable but links 404.

diagnosis: Com.Method.Utils.TimeZoneLookup.GetSystemTimeZoneById(tzID) (legacy-common-core Method.Common/Com.Method/Utils/TimeZoneLookup.cs, line ~939) maps friendly names (EASTERN/CENTRAL/PACIFIC) to Windows tz ids, but its default case calls TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById(tzID) directly. On the Windows classic hosts (PROD-CLASSIC-01/02) an IANA tz id such as 'America/New_York' is not a valid Windows id, so FindSystemTimeZoneById throws System.TimeZoneNotFoundException. Every caller (GetUtcOffset/IsDst/etc., lines ~189-312) expects null on an unknown id ('if (tz == null) return -1') rather than an exception, so the throw is unhandled and logged. 2026-06-17 19:08-20:10Z: 396 errors, 95% account=thestoragegroup (378), supplyshield (18), both PROD-CLASSIC-01 (200) + PROD-CLASSIC-02 (196); actions fncNativeFieldDateAndTime (288), fncConverFromUTCTime (70), fncConverToUTCTime (38). Account-data driven: the affected account's stored timezone value is an IANA id, not a Windows id or a friendly name.
playbook: 1) IMMEDIATE mitigation (no deploy): correct the stored timezone for the dominant account(s) (thestoragegroup, supplyshield) from the IANA id 'America/New_York' to the Windows id 'Eastern Standard Time' (or the friendly 'EASTERN' the switch already handles) in the account's classic timezone setting. This stops 95%+ of the volume. 2) DURABLE code fix (legacy-common-core TimeZoneLookup.GetSystemTimeZoneById default case): wrap FindSystemTimeZoneById in try/catch(TimeZoneNotFoundException); on failure, best-effort map common IANA ids -> Windows ids (America/New_York->Eastern Standard Time, America/Chicago->Central Standard Time, America/Denver->Mountain Standard Time, America/Los_Angeles->Pacific Standard Time) and otherwise return null to honour the existing caller null-contract. Single-file, ~18 lines. 3) Verify post-fix: ES query 'TimeZoneNotFoundException' over the classic indices should drop to ~0. 4) Note: classic deploys via TFS (invisible to git/gh) — confirm rollout with the classic deploy owner.

diagnosis: Method.Import.Api /newimport/health/check returned HTTP 503 (overall status 'Unhealthy') on BOTH import hosts (MSL03, MSL04) at 2026-06-27T08:44-08:48Z. title: ms-scheduler-api GetSeriesAsync throws InvalidOperationException when called with recordId=-1 (chronic, code-level missing-guard bug, now confirmed across multiple accounts, ~10-21+/day for 7+ days)

any_of.contains: Failed to Get Series Id for record -1

evidence_query: fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND exceptions.Message.keyword:"Failed to Get Series Id for record -1 in table Activity"
diagnosis: ms-scheduler-api's SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync (Scheduler.Core) is called with recordId=-1 for account lafittesseafood via API.Controllers.SeriesController.GetSeriesAsync (RequestPath /v1/series/getseries). The provider queries SQL expecting a row for that record and does not guard against the sentinel/invalid recordId=-1 before reading; SqlDataReader.GetValue() then throws System.InvalidOperationException ('Invalid attempt to read when no data is present'), which surfaces as System.Exception('Failed to Get Series Id for record -1 in table Activity'). ES confirms 125 identical occurrences over the last 7 days (2026-06-26 to 2026-07-03), steady daily volume (10-21/day), single account, single stack trace -- a chronic pre-existing bug, not a new incident. DD's '[CRM] ms-scheduler-api error rate high' monitor (302054543) is a newly-observed monitor that tripped for the first time today only because this service's low overall traffic makes its error-rate percentage sensitive to a handful of absolute errors (6 errors / 233 hits = 2.56% vs 2% threshold in the trigger window) -- the underlying bug itself did not spike. UPDATE 2026-07-03T21:08Z: this cycle's ES recurrence check (13:04:37Z–21:08:31Z window) found 21 new identical-signature events spanning 6 distinct accounts (completeelectricalsolutions:8, foamtechinc:7, refexpertsandhvacllc:3, cooksmart2:1, farmxs:1, lafittesseafood:1) — lafittesseafood is now the smallest contributor, not the sole one. This upgrades the diagnosis from a single-account client/data issue to a code-level defect: SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync does not guard recordId=-1 before calling SqlDataReader.GetValue(), and reproduces for ANY account whose caller passes the -1 sentinel. Root cause location unchanged (SeriesDataProvider.cs:143 call site, :123 throw site; SeriesController.cs:100 entry point).
playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD monitor 302054543 in 'Alert' state, OR ES query fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND fields.Account.keyword:"lafittesseafood" returning the 'Failed to Get Series Id for record -1' signature. 2) Compute the error-rate ratio in DD (errors/hits over the alert's own last_10m window) -- historically marginal (~2.5%), not a severe spike; do not over-escalate on the DD monitor state alone. 3) The root cause is a code-level missing-guard bug in SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync (not account-specific) -- as of 2026-07-03T21:08Z it has reproduced across 6 distinct accounts, not just lafittesseafood. Still not infra-wide (no elevated volume, no user-facing impact beyond scattered per-account 500s), but do not describe it as single-account going forward. 4) File/bump a defect for CRM Experience (#team-customer-management) rather than re-diagnosing from scratch each cycle.

title: New team:crm AMQP-consumer heartbeat/throughput-stall monitors (5 sibling IDs, created 2026-07-02) intermittently trip on quiet-period low-traffic dips, then self-recover within minutes — no corroborating errors
evidence_query: avg(last_15m or last_20m per-monitor):sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:<fired-service>,env:prod}.as_rate() < <per-monitor threshold ~2 msg/s for throughput checks, ~0.005 msg/s for heartbeat checks> — re-run scripts/dd_search.py metric with the specific fired monitor's own query over a multi-hour window; expect near-threshold values immediately pre-trigger and a fast return to normal, plus 0 hits on `service:<name> status:error` in DD Logs for the same window.
diagnosis: Five sibling DD monitors under a 2-day-old (created 2026-07-02) team:crm AMQP-consumer monitor rollout — email-subscriber-agent heartbeat (302055017), email-publisher-agent heartbeat (302055075), method-mobile-notifications-subscriber heartbeat (302055141), approutine-subscriber heartbeat (302055190), and runtime-core-subscriber throughput (302057011) — all check `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:<name>,env:prod}.as_rate()` against a low absolute floor (~2 msg/s for the 'throughput dropped' checks, ~0.005 msg/s for the 'consumer silent' heartbeat checks). Two of the five have fired so far, both on 2026-07-04: runtime-core-subscriber (302057011) 3x — 13:07:31Z (first-ever, see docs/investigations/2026-07-04-89729b4fe24c5575.md), 15:10:31Z (2nd, docs/investigations/2026-07-04-74e56115ec846ca1.md), 16:05:31Z (3rd, this cycle) — and method-mobile-notifications-subscriber (302055141) 2x — 14:29:21Z (first, discovered retroactively this cycle via baseline-scan diff, never individually investigated) and 15:48:21Z (2nd, this cycle). All 5 occurrences share the same shape: DD metric shows a genuine dip below the monitor's floor for a period of minutes to tens of minutes, 0 hits on `service:<name> status:error` in DD Logs for the corresponding window, no sibling 5xx/latency monitor co-firing, and a fast self-recovery (state back to OK within roughly 5–50 minutes, no cycle has caught one still open). Deploy-correlation is unconfirmed for all 5 — methodcrm/runtime-core (and by extension any shared subscriber-host code) is blocked by a known GH_TOKEN 403/404 gap on this org's private repos, re-confirmed each occurrence. Working theory: these two services are genuinely low-volume AMQP consumers (method-mobile-notifications-subscriber's raw metric shows only ~35 datapoints across a 3h13m window — mostly silent minutes are normal for it), so an absolute-floor rate threshold with no allowance for natural quiet periods will trip repeatedly without any actual stall or customer impact. Not yet confirmed against source code (no access to the actual subscriber-host repos to check whether 'silent' means 'idle/healthy' vs 'crashed and not reconnecting' — CLAUDE.md's documented runtime-core failure mode 'Cache stale → Subscriber down → Start Subscriber.Agent' remains a live alternative explanation the bot cannot rule out without SSH/host access). title: [Rainforest] Outbound API P95 Latency > 3s -- runtime-core-api outbound calls to api.rainforestpay.com intermittently breach 3s p95, self-recovering, zero corroborating errors (third-party latency, not a Method-side defect)
evidence_query: percentile(last_10m):p95:trace.http.request{env:prod,peer.hostname:api.rainforestpay.com} > 3 -- re-run scripts/dd_search.py metric with the same scope over a wide window; expect a sparse series (low-volume on-demand integration) with 0-2 datapoints near the trigger and 0 hits on service:runtime-core-api status:error in DD Logs for the same window.
diagnosis: DD monitor 295928665 ('[Rainforest] Outbound API P95 Latency > 3s', service:runtime-core-api, team:transactions, severity:p2, integration:rainforest) checks p95 latency on Method's outbound HTTP calls to the third-party Rainforest payment API (api.rainforestpay.com). 2 occurrences to date, both 2026-07-05: 1st at 08:31:25Z (peak p95 7.16s independently confirmed via direct metric query, docs/investigations/2026-07-05-63bf5b7a3ac9f93a.md, posted to #triage-results at escalation_score 7), 2nd at 15:08:26Z (nearest reproducible value 2.29s max, just under threshold -- the exact in-window breach value could not be independently reproduced due to extremely sparse data, docs/investigations/2026-07-05-130dcdd3332d05e5.md). Both occurrences share the same shape: the metric series is sparse (consistent with Rainforest being a low-volume, on-demand integration -- calls only happen when a customer transaction triggers one), 0 hits on service:runtime-core-api status:error in DD Logs for the corresponding window, no deploy correlation available (methodcrm-org GH_TOKEN 403 gap, standing), and a fast self-recovery (OK by scan time both times). This is Method's OUTBOUND call latency to a third-party payment processor -- nothing in Method's own code path to fix, analogous to ki-shuttle-third-party-platform-outage (a different third-party payment platform with its own recurring-outage KB entry). This monitor's real Slack channel is #alert-transactions, which is NOT in kb/config.json.channels (see memory project_alert_transactions_gap) -- only caught via the full DD monitor scan during degraded (no-Slack-MCP) cycles or a proactive monitor sweep.
playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor 295928665, p95 latency query on peer.hostname:api.rainforestpay.com. 2) Pull scripts/dd_search.py metric over a wide window (data is sparse -- widen to +/-1h if the exact trigger window returns nothing) -- expect a real but brief latency elevation, not a tooling failure. 3) Confirm service:runtime-core-api status:error returns 0 in DD Logs for the window -- if errors ARE present, this is no longer a pure latency blip and should be escalated as a possible payment-failure incident, not filed under this entry. 4) Root cause is third-party (Rainforest infrastructure) -- no Method-side code fix. If it recurs with high frequency or errors start appearing, escalate to Ben to check Rainforest status/support channel and consider whether Method needs a timeout/retry/circuit-breaker adjustment on this integration.

title: runtime-core-api Rainforest GetMerchantAsync (merchant-details lookup) fails with ServiceUnavailable when Rainforest's own API returns a 503 -- third-party payment-processor degradation, not a Method-side defect
diagnosis: DD monitor 295882732 ('[Rainforest] Outbound API Error Rate (4xx+5xx) > 5%', service:runtime-core-api, team:transactions) tripped to Alert at 13:03:52Z. ES confirms 2 Error-level log hits at 13:02:25Z, both for account totalfeedsinc (single user session, RequestId 2e6a5940): 'Rainforest Merchant Details Retrieval Failed' -> System.InvalidOperationException('Rainforest API returned status code: ServiceUnavailable') at Runtime.Core.Engine.Actions.Payments.PaymentsV2.Providers.RainforestProvider.GetMerchantAsync (RainforestProvider.cs:286), called from PaymentService.GetRainforestMerchantDetailsAsync (PaymentService.Rainforest.cs:868) via PaymentsController.GetRainforestMerchantDetailsAsync (PaymentsController.Rainforest.cs:391). The 503 originates from Rainforest's own API (peer.hostname:api.rainforestpay.com), not from Method code -- runtime-core-api's dd_version (2026-06-30 14-37-master) is 6 days old, no deploy correlation. Sibling monitor 295882894 ('[Rainforest] Webhook Traffic Outage (Business Hours)') co-fired 2min51s earlier (13:01:01Z, recovered to OK by scan time) -- consistent with a brief window where Rainforest's platform was degraded broadly (both outbound API calls and inbound webhook delivery affected), not specific to the merchant-details endpoint. Same third-party-dependency framing as ki-2026-07-05-rainforest-outbound-api-p95-latency (that entry covers P95 latency on monitor 295928665; this is a distinct monitor/signal -- error rate, not latency -- so a separate entry, not a match broaden, given the current evidence doesn't establish they share a single root-cause mechanism beyond 'Rainforest degradation').
playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD monitor 295882732 in Alert, OR ES query fields.dd_service.keyword:"runtime-core-api" AND message:*rainforest* returning 'ServiceUnavailable' / 'Rainforest API returned status code' signatures. 2) Check monitor 295882894 (Webhook Traffic Outage) and monitor 295928665 (Outbound API P95 Latency, see ki-2026-07-05-rainforest-outbound-api-p95-latency) for co-firing in the same window -- if so, broaden framing to 'Rainforest platform degradation', not endpoint-specific. 3) Nothing to fix Method-side; this is entirely dependent on Rainforest's own uptime. 4) If sustained (>15min) or affecting >1 account, consider paging Transactions team to check Rainforest's status page / support channel; a single brief blip like this occurrence does not warrant escalation beyond logging.

diagnosis: Deleting a field/column (API.Controllers.FieldController.SaveFieldLegacyExtended -> ViewService.EditView -> ViewService.DeleteFields -> FieldService.TryDeleteField -> FieldService.DeleteFieldByTableAndFieldName -> ColumnService.DeleteColumn -> TableService.AlterTableToDropColumn -> TableProvider.AlterTableToDropColumn) builds a raw SQL batch via string interpolation: `query.Append($" ALTER TABLE {tableName} DROP COLUMN {columnName} ");` (Services/Providers/TableProvider.cs, local clone HEAD 2026-04-24 -- 73 days stale, methodcrm-org GH_TOKEN 403 blocks a fresh fetch this session, so the current line number/content is NOT independently confirmed against production). evidence_query: sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits{env:prod,service:designer-core-api}.as_count() -- re-run over the fire's 30-40min pre-fire window; the monitor itself is a weekly-seasonality anomaly detector (avg(last_4h):anomalies(sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits{env:prod,service:designer-core-api}.as_count(), 'agile', 3, direction='both', interval=60, alert_window='last_15m', seasonality='weekly', timezone='utc', count_default_zero='true') >= 1) whose own baseline band isn't exposed by dd_search.py metric -- the absolute-count query is a proxy, not the detector's actual signal.
evidence_note: Anomaly-detector-sourced, not a fixed-threshold breach -- there is no single number to compare against. Confirm the shape (steady low-absolute traffic 1-10 hits/20s bucket, no visible spike/drop near the fire timestamp) and 0 error logs. Do NOT build a Kibana log link unless a 3rd occurrence actually surfaces an ES/error signal.
diagnosis: DD monitor 115452625 ('Service designer-core-api has an abnormal change in throughput on env:prod', team:poiesis) uses a weekly-seasonality anomaly detector on request-hit count. Both documented occurrences (2026-07-10T09:53:25Z and 2026-07-12T14:11:26Z) show the same shape: designer-core-api serves low absolute traffic (roughly 1-10 requests per 20s bucket), 0 error logs, 0 ES hits, and no visible spike or drop in the raw count around the fire timestamp. Most likely a low-traffic-window false-positive from the relative-deviation anomaly algorithm rather than a genuine throughput incident -- same theory as the ki-2026-07-04/07-07 monitor-noise sibling entries, though the detector's own baseline band was not directly queryable either time, so this remains unconfirmed rather than proven.
playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor 115452625 in Alert (or recently-recovered) state. 2) Run `dd_search.py metric --query 'sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits{env:prod,service:designer-core-api}.as_count()'` over the fire's pre-fire window -- expect steady low counts (1-10/20s bucket), no dramatic absolute change at the fire timestamp. 3) Check `service:designer-core-api status:error env:prod` DD Logs -- expect 0 hits, consistent with both documented occurrences. 4) If a future occurrence instead shows a real absolute spike/drop or a nonzero error signal, treat as a break from this pattern and escalate immediately rather than assuming noise -- this entry has only 2 occurrences, thinner evidence than the sibling monitor-noise entries.

title: Cross-service P95 latency correlated spike (runtime-core RTC, classic/method, ms-search-api, miurl) -- shared-upstream, latency-only, self-recovering

match.precedence_note: Do NOT broad-match on bare "miurl" or "ms-search" substrings -- "miurl" bare-matches ki-2026-06-16-miurl-shortlink-domain-unreachable (DNS/domain-resolution issue, unrelated mechanism) and ki-2026-07-04-miurl-5xx-monitor-noise (different monitor 302048068, 5xx error rate not p95 latency); "ms-search" bare-matches ki-stockapp-ms-search-cpu-contention-msn-crash (resolved 2025-01-02 CPU-contention/host-crash incident, unrelated mechanism -- host CPU was independently checked and ruled out for this entry's 2026-07-14 occurrence). Confirm the exact monitor id (302048329 or 299551623) or the literal "P95 latency high (...)" text before accepting a match against this entry. First occurrence (2026-07-14) co-fired with ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring (monitors 115456700/117279738) and ki-2026-07-07-classicmethod-p95-latency-monitor-recurring (monitor 299603201) -- all 5 monitors elevated simultaneously across the SAME ~17:36-18:05Z sustained window, confirmed via each service's own underlying APM metric series, not just alert-timestamp proximity. Treat a co-fire with any of those 3 entries as this same expanded shared-upstream signature. 2026-07-29 ~16:39Z REFUTED MATCH: monitor 302048329 fired 16:39:49Z, hash 52adfd150c9d0883, co-firing in the same rough window as ki-24 (115456700 @ 16:38:20Z, 117279738 @ 16:41:18Z) -- the co-fire TIMING condition that normally indicates this shared-upstream signature was met, but the MAGNITUDE evidence flatly failed to corroborate: p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:miurl,env:prod} over the monitor's own exact eval window (16:29:49-16:39:49Z, avg(last_10m)) showed a peak of only 0.50s against this entry's 2.0s evidence_threshold (0/60 points over threshold) -- nowhere near the 07-14 occurrence's peak of 56.32s. Traffic was NOT sparse (1522 hits in the window), so this isn't the usual low-traffic-percentile-artifact excuse either -- genuinely unexplained discrepancy between what tripped the monitor's own evaluator and what the metrics query API returns for the identical window/query. No occurrence bump. Logged as a fresh, low-signal needs-human finding instead (hash 52adfd150c9d0883, appended to docs/actionable/2026-07-29.md, score below escalation threshold).

evidence_note: Two distinct monitor queries share the same 2.0s threshold. Latency-only / APM-sourced -- miurl is not ES-instrumented at all (legacy .NET Framework); ms-search-api's small volume of ES errors during any given window has so far been unrelated user-input validation noise, not an infra signal. Corroborate via DD: run both evidence queries (count points > 2.0s, note peak + timestamp), confirm 0 errors via dd_search.py logs on both services, and check whether ki-24 / classicmethod monitors are ALSO elevated in the same window (the defining feature of this entry).
diagnosis: First observed 2026-07-14: DD monitors 302048329 ([VAE][miurl][P2] P95 latency high, threshold 2.0s) and 299551623 ([Admin][SearchAPI][P2] P95 latency high, threshold 2.0s) breached simultaneously with runtime-core-api's RTC p95 monitors (115456700/117279738, threshold 3.0s) and classic/method's p95 monitor (299603201, threshold 20.0s) during a sustained ~29-minute window (17:36-18:05Z). Peaks: miurl 56.32s (ratio 27.16x), ms-search-api 22.22s (ratio 10.11x). Zero error-log signal on any of the 4 services (0 status:error DD logs across the board). The only corroborating error signal anywhere is a weak cluster of 4 "Redis operation cancelled" (Runtime.Caching.CacheContext) errors on runtime-core-api, diffuse across 4 unrelated accounts -- consistent with but not conclusive of the existing ki-24 Redis-backpressure hypothesis, and does not obviously explain classic/method or miurl (legacy IIS apps not known to share runtime-core's Redis cache). Host CPU checked across all runtime-core/classic/msl/svc hosts and ruled out (peak 19.2%, well below saturation) -- rules out a repeat of the ki-stockapp-ms-search-cpu-contention-msn-crash mechanism. No co-firing SQL/Mongo/Redis/gateway/DNS monitor. No deploy correlation available (methodcrm-org GH_TOKEN 403 gap blocks all 4 candidate repos). All 5 monitors self-recovered without intervention by ~18:06-18:08Z. Breadth (4 independently-deployed codebases spanning 3 owning teams: Admin, Vertical App Experience, Transactions) makes an application-code-level cause on any single service unlikely -- root cause is most probably shared infrastructure (network path, load balancer, DNS, or a datastore/cache shared more broadly than previously scoped) but is NOT identified. DD APM trace search (not wired into dd_search.py) would be needed to pinpoint the actual shared span.
playbook: 1) On monitors 302048329 (miurl P95>2s) or 299551623 (ms-search-api P95>2s) firing, first check whether ki-24 (115456700/117279738) and/or the classicmethod monitor (299603201) are ALSO in Alert/recently-triggered in the same window -- if so, this is the shared-upstream signature, not two independent service-specific issues. 2) Re-run p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:miurl,env:prod} and p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{service:ms-search-api,env:prod} over the window; note point-count over 2.0s threshold, peak, and span. 3) Confirm latency-only: status:error DD Logs on all co-firing services should be ~0. 4) Check ES for "Redis operation cancelled" / Runtime.Caching.CacheContext on runtime-core-api in the same window -- weak but real corroboration of a shared caching/Redis dependency. 5) Check per-host CPU (runtime.dotnet.cpu.percent) across prod-rt-*/prod-classic-*/prod-msl-*/prod-svc-* -- if elevated, suspect a repeat of the ki-stockapp CPU-contention pattern instead (different root cause; check for a co-located StockApp/tables-fields release). 6) No fix identified yet -- if this recurs, escalate to Admin/VAE/Transactions jointly (the co-firing services span 3 different owning teams) to investigate a shared dependency: load balancer, DNS resolution path, or a common backing datastore. No single team owns enough of the picture to root-cause this alone.

title: App Update push of template app 'Sales Orders' v182 fails on ~196 accounts with 400 ErrorCode 50 "The field 'Name' already exists" on view InvSalesOrderRevertReason -- leaves partial schema (preference field created, target table missing); the ~5,500-account fan-out is also a 4.5x load storm on ms-tables-fields-api

match.precedence_note: Do NOT match this entry on the collateral monitor ids alone (299251779 tables-fields p95, 227940275 Redis errors, 115456700 RTC screen load) -- those three bare-match OTHER entries and all three are wrong for this incident. The discriminator is an 'App Publish - Started' event in ES service:app-update-agent within ~5 min BEFORE the monitor fires. Conversely: if tables-fields p95 fires with NO preceding App Publish event, this is NOT this entry -- check ki-2026-07-06-tables-fields-redis-circuitbreaker-p95-latency (Redis blip precedes the spike) instead. RTC screen load (115456700) fires independently of this entry (see ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring, 238 occurrences) -- on 2026-07-15 it triggered 8 min BEFORE the push and continued after it ended; never fold it into this entry's blast radius without checking the ordering.

evidence_note: ES-sourced. The authoritative trigger event is fields.dd_service.keyword:"app-update-agent" AND messageTemplate.keyword:*App Publish - Started* -- it carries AppCaption, AppVersion, JobId and PublisherAccount. Aggregate the error query by fields.Account.keyword to enumerate the exact failed-account population (the job's own log lines ARE the complete population -- no extrapolation needed). Corroborate the load story with DD metric sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits{env:prod,service:tables-fields}.as_count() vs the same window 24h earlier.
diagnosis: 2026-07-15 13:13:13.53Z: 'App Publish - Started - Push Update [App: "Sales Orders", AppId: 55b7fa26-9d45-400d-829f-a3610098567c, Version: 182, JobId: d055f8dd-9bb5-4996-9d71-dd7bae39c557, Publisher: "templatedevv2"]' (SourceContext Runtime.AppUpdate.Agent.Update.PublishAppCommand). Fan-out to ~5,571 subscriber accounts over ~27 min (13:13->13:40Z): 5,292 completed, 170 failed, 539 skipped (opted out). TWO distinct consequences. (1) FUNCTIONAL, deterministic: 196 distinct accounts failed, 179 with HTTP 400 ErrorCode 50 'The field Name already exists. Please change the spelling and try again.' on view InvSalesOrderRevertReason (+15 'data misaligned', e.g. 'Can not add field Job of Type Text to SalesOrder because source type is DropDown'). v182 introduces the InvSalesOrderRevertReason view/table plus a DefaultInvSalesOrderRevertReason preference field on viewPreferencesMethod; on the failing accounts the bundle's declared field 'Name' collides with a 'Name' that already exists on that view. The bundle applies NON-ATOMICALLY -- the API response shows SuccessfulBundle=[viewPreferencesMethod -> DefaultInvSalesOrderRevertReason created] while UnSuccessfulBundle=[InvSalesOrderRevertReason failed], so those accounts are left with a preference pointing at a table that does not exist, and there is no rollback. Root cause of the collision itself (fresh-table bootstrap auto-creating 'Name' vs a pre-existing customization / leftover table) is NOT yet established -- needs a tenant-DB read. (2) COLLATERAL LOAD: the un-throttled fan-out drove ms-tables-fields-api to 4.5x normal volume (58,036 requests 11:00-16:00Z vs 12,817 in the same window on 07-14; peak 4,182/bucket @13:28Z vs 802 yesterday), p95 peak 3.25s (median 0.059s, 29 buckets >1s, 13:13->13:41Z) with post_/v1/field/saveviewbundleinternal p95 at 10.72s -- this is what fired monitor 299251779. Redis is an EFFECT, not a cause: first SaveViewBundleInternal failure 13:13:17.21Z, first 'Redis Cache Circuit Breaker OPENED' 13:13:27.74Z (10s LATER); all 11 opens sit inside the push window; trace.redis.command.errors by service = tables-fields 41 / nonprod-apps 6 / syncapi 1 / runtime-core-api 0 -- which fired monitor 227940275. tables-fields fully recovered by 14:00Z (peak 0.62s, 0/180 buckets >1s). PRIOR ART: the Sales Orders v181 push (2026-07-08 16:13:54Z, job 1e302df5) produced the same storm at 1/3 scale (15,294 hits, p95 peak 1.57s, 1 bucket >1s) without crossing thresholds -- mass push fan-out is a routine, escalating load event, not a one-off.
playbook: 1) Confirm the trigger: python scripts/es_search.py search --query 'fields.dd_service.keyword:"app-update-agent" AND messageTemplate.keyword:*App Publish - Started*' --from <alert-30m> --to <alert> -- if there is no App Publish event, this is NOT this entry (see precedence_note). 2) Enumerate the damage: python scripts/es_search.py aggregate --query 'fields.dd_service.keyword:"app-update-agent" AND level.keyword:"Error" AND fields.AppId.keyword:"<appid>"' --from <push> --to <push+45m> --field fields.Account.keyword --top 400 -- the bucket count IS the failed-account population. 3) Classify failure modes from fields.ErrorMessage: '<field> already exists' (ErrorCode 50) = view/field collision; 'because source type is DropDown' = data-misaligned. 4) Check for partial application: read the API response body in the alert -- if SuccessfulBundle is non-empty while UnSuccessfulBundle is non-empty, those accounts are in a SPLIT schema state and re-running the push will NOT fix them (same collision). Escalate for reconciliation. 5) Confirm the load story: DD metric sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits{env:prod,service:tables-fields}.as_count() for the window vs 24h earlier. 6) Do NOT attribute RTC screen load (115456700) to the push without checking whether it breached BEFORE the App Publish timestamp -- on the first occurrence it did. 7) Owning team (identify only, never tag): app-update-agent -> CRM Experience (@customer-management / #team-customer-management); Sales Orders app content -> Vertical App Experience (@sales management / #team-sales-management); ms-tables-fields-api -> Admin (@admin / #team-admin).
notes: Follow-ups: (a) make bundle application atomic or roll back SuccessfulBundle entries on partial failure -- highest-value fix; (b) throttle/stagger the push consumer (~5,500 accounts in 27 min = 4.5x load on a critical-path service, and it grows with the subscriber base); (c) reconcile the 196 accounts left on v181 content + a v182 preference field; (d) NO monitor exists on app-update job failure rate -- 196 accounts failed and every monitor that fired named the wrong service.

title: ms-tables-fields-api EditView view-regeneration fails after retry (System.Exception 'Failed to generate view {X} after retry') -- 4th distinct bug class on monitor 299251404

match.precedence_note: 2026-07-28: DD monitor 299251404 ('Service tables-fields has a high error rate') fired again but the ES message.keyword buckets were 'Table View Creation Failed' (8), 'EditView ViewGen failed after retry...' (4), and 'SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed' (4) -- all 4 underlying trace_ids share this one cascade, NOT ki-2026-07-02 (FieldTableNameRef Is Null), ki-2026-07-06 (AlterTableToDropColumn/Incorrect syntax near COLUMN), or ki-2026-07-09/ki-2026-07-11 (duplicate-key ShippingAddress / HelperConverter.GetFields NRE -- note this entry's 'SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed' bucket text is IDENTICAL to ki-2026-07-11's any_of clause; the two are distinguished ONLY by exception type -- this entry's exceptions[0].StackTraceString shows Services.Views.ViewService.EditView (ViewService.cs:394) throwing System.Exception, ki-2026-07-11's shows Models.Converters.HelperConverter.GetFields throwing NullReferenceException. ALWAYS read the full exceptions[0].StackTraceString before accepting either match -- a bare 'SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed' text match is not sufficient (5th trap on this monitor, see feedback_kb_bare_monitor_id_false_match precedent).

diagnosis: API.Controllers.FieldController.SaveFieldLegacyExtended -> Services.Views.ViewService.EditView (ViewService.cs:~383) calls TryGenerateView, which wraps ViewProvider.GenerateView in a try/catch-retry-once (200ms sleep) pattern (ViewService.cs:502-525). ViewProvider.GenerateView (ViewProvider.cs:310-329) calls the legacy SyncServicesHelper.fnCreateViewFromTableName(db, tableName, ...); when that returns a non-'Success' syncMessage, it logs 'Table View Creation Failed' (table/mode/error as unstructured positional log args -- NOT indexed as separate ES fields, an observability gap: the actual syncMessage/error text is not queryable) and throws. After both the initial attempt and the single retry fail, TryGenerateView returns false; EditView (ViewService.cs:390-394) logs the Error-level 'EditView ViewGen failed after retry; metadata for new fields is already committed and the view does not reflect it. spiderColumns/spiderColumnsMultiSelect/spiderViewFields/Bridge_* rows may be orphaned.' and throws System.Exception('Failed to generate view {FriendlyName} after retry.'), caught and re-logged by the controller as 'SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed'. This cycle: 4 distinct dd_trace_ids in a 28s window (17:41:49-17:42:17Z), 2 for view 'Customer' and 2 for view 'Entity' -- all field-add/edit operations against the same two core entity views. Root cause of WHY fnCreateViewFromTableName fails is not traced this session (legacy SyncServicesHelper, no stack trace surfaces past ViewProvider.GenerateView's own throw -- the original inner failure is not logged as an InnerException). No account/tenant identifier is present in any of the three log lines' indexed fields (db/account are passed as unstructured positional args, not indexed) -- account impact could not be resolved via account_impact.py this cycle.
playbook: 1) Confirm via ES message.keyword agg for tables-fields/level:Error -- if buckets are 'Table View Creation Failed' + 'EditView ViewGen failed after retry...' + 'SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed' together (co-occurring on the same dd_trace_id), this is the entry. 2) Pull the 'SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed' sample's exceptions[0].StackTraceString -- confirm ClassName System.Exception, message 'Failed to generate view {X} after retry', origin Services.Views.ViewService.EditView (ViewService.cs:394) -- if instead ClassName is System.NullReferenceException at HelperConverter.GetFields, that's ki-2026-07-11, not this entry. 3) The db/tenant is not captured in indexed ES fields for this signature -- if account impact matters, the fix should also add db/account as an indexed structured field (not a raw positional log arg) to close this observability gap. 4) Root cause is inside the legacy SyncServicesHelper.fnCreateViewFromTableName -- needs-human to trace further (methodcrm-org GH_TOKEN access gap blocked a fresh fetch this session; local ms-tables-fields-api clone last confirmed at d5a7e25 2026-07-06).

title: billingengine-api subscription pages 500 on Sunday after Friday release removed API key1 used by nightly billing agent
diagnosis: billingengine-api historically supported two API keys (key1 and key2). A recent AI-assisted refactor removed key1, unaware that the nightly billing agent depended on it while the subscription page used key2. Friday's release passed regression because subscription page traffic uses key2. Saturday morning the nightly billing agent failed because it needed key1. As a workaround, key1 was replaced with key2 in production to rerun billing, which then broke the subscription page (500 error in browser console) starting Sunday. Mitigation: rolled back the Friday billingengine-api release.
playbook: 1) Confirm: subscription page 500s for Method:New customers + recent billingengine-api release in last few days. 2) Check whether a billing agent run failed overnight (look for key1/key2 references in billing agent logs). 3) Mitigation: roll back the most recent billingengine-api release. 4) Long-term per PIR action items: establish dependency-identification procedure before release, expand regression coverage to cover billing-agent-driven flows, avoid Friday billing-related releases since failures surface only Saturday/Sunday morning.

title: Calendar Sync deploy fails health check when project targets a .NET Framework version the server doesn't have installed
diagnosis: On 2026-05-06 the Google Calendar Sync deployment failed its health check ~14 minutes after it started and was rolled back. Root cause: the project had been upgraded to target .NET Framework 4.8, but the target server didn't have 4.8 installed, so the service couldn't start. This pattern recurs whenever a .NET Framework version bump is made without first confirming the runtime is installed on every machine in the IIS pool.
playbook: 1) On deploy failure for a .NET Framework service, check the targeted TargetFrameworkVersion in the csproj that was deployed vs. installed .NET Framework versions on the target machines (`Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\NET Framework Setup\NDP'`). 2) If mismatched, roll back the deploy (the standard outcome here). 3) Long-term per PIR: any .NET Framework version bump must be coordinated with DevOps to confirm the framework is installed on every target server before merging.

title: Chrome update on Windows sporadically breaks Method Screen Editor template loading (PL-44761)
diagnosis: A new Chrome release on Windows sporadically broke the Method Screen Editor — could not view Properties or Action Sets of screen controls. Root cause: Method's designer template-loading logic interacted with a behavior change introduced in the latest Chrome update. No known customer impact (P2 ticket). Pattern is durable: any future Chrome update can recur this kind of break on the designer.
playbook: 1) On 'Screen Editor / Designer broken on Chrome' reports — especially clustered in a single browser version — check the Chrome release notes for changes touching DOM/iframe/template loading. 2) Confirm by reproducing in a different Chrome version or another browser (Edge/Firefox). 3) Mitigation: workaround for users (older Chrome, or different browser). 4) Long-term: instrument designer template-loading against Chrome beta channel for early detection.

title: Classic users can't sign in after CLB→ALB switch because IIS SSL redirect rules weren't carried over
diagnosis: DevOps replaced the Classic load balancers (CLB → ALB). The new ALB setup did not initially account for the IIS redirect rules that route Classic to external servers via SSL, so fresh sign-ins broke. Existing/cached sessions weren't affected, which delayed detection — ~7 Classic accounts hit the issue before the change was rolled back within a minute of detection. Browser caching meant users continued to see the issue for several minutes after rollback. Fix: added an SSL certificate to the new ALB that evening, plus a separate target group for HTTPS traffic to handle secure redirects.
playbook: 1) On 'page loading' / 'stuck during sign-in' for Classic users immediately after a load-balancer or routing change, check whether IIS SSL redirect rules are intact on the new LB. 2) Confirm via the cache signal: fresh sign-ins fail but already-signed-in users work — this is the LB-change fingerprint. 3) Mitigation: roll back the LB change. 4) Long-term: when migrating CLB→ALB, ensure SSL cert + separate HTTPS target group + IIS redirect rules are all migrated; never make such changes during business hours.

title: Classic users stuck at account-selection screen because time desync between Classic and new auth servers expires tokens prematurely
diagnosis: 20+ Classic users on multiple accounts (cornerstonetf, cdsanalytical, customequipmentcompanyinc, etc.) could not proceed past the account-selection screen when signing into Classic. The issue was reproducible in regular Chrome but not Incognito, indicating cached-state interaction with a real backend problem. Root cause: time desynchronization between Classic and new auth servers caused valid tokens to be rejected as expired. After syncing the clocks on the two machines, affected users were able to sign in without clearing cache. Long-term: Classic is migrating to Windows Server 2022, which should keep clocks in sync via the standard NTP setup.
playbook: 1) On 'cannot proceed past account selection' Classic sign-in reports, check time synchronization between the Classic auth machines and the new auth servers (run `w32tm /query /status` on each Windows host). 2) Confirm via the workaround: Incognito works, regular Chrome doesn't — that's the signal. 3) Mitigation: run `w32tm /resync` on the affected servers to bring time back in sync. 4) Long-term: complete Classic's migration to Windows Server 2022 (this is the canonical fix per the PIR).

title: Classic UI app pool crashes from EDA NuGet async-call thread starvation on .NET Framework
diagnosis: Classic UI IIS app pools crash intermittently under high EDA load. Root cause: new EDA NuGet package's asynchronous calls cause thread starvation in older .NET Framework code paths (known limitation in pre-modern .NET). Datadog tracer upgrades and older MassTransit libraries amplify the problem. Load test confirmed: the async version of the NuGet crashes after ~500-600 calls returning 502s; the sync version survives 1000 calls with ~62 timeouts but no crash. Mitigations applied: reduced EDA load and redeployed prior stable code (night of 2026-05-04). A modified sync-only NuGet exists; deployment postponed pending stability.
playbook: 1) Check IIS Event Viewer on PROD-CLASSIC-01/02 for app-pool crashes. 2) Confirm via the absence of explicit error stacks â€” Classic crashes here typically show only pool crashes with no application stack trace. 3) Look at EDA event rate; if elevated, this is the pattern. 4) Mitigation: recycle app pools, or reduce EDA event volume (reduce accounts producing events), or roll back to prior NuGet/Datadog tracer state. 5) Long-term fix is the sync-only NuGet package (built by Matt) â€” deployment pending.

title: Compromised customer account sends mass spam through Method's SendGrid → Yahoo/AOL IP block → fallback email delivery degraded (recurring: PL-49712, PL-52097)
diagnosis: Recurring pattern: a customer login is compromised (password reuse across sites; Method's rate-limit doesn't slow a single-attempt brute-force) and the attacker uses the account to send tens of thousands of crypto/scam emails through Method's shared SendGrid sub-user. Yahoo / AOL detect the volume + content and block the sending IPs; SendGrid eventually suspends the sub-user. Method's mitigation pattern: detect via automated alert (~1h after attack start), disable logins on the offending account, transition the marketing fallback to a new sub-user, rotate IPs, add a code-level block for the offending account, set hard rate limits temporarily (e.g., 100 marketing / 500 transactional). Customer impact: all customers without an authenticated custom domain temporarily can't send to Yahoo/AOL. Confirmed events: soldiersports (Oct 25 2024, 90k+ spam emails, IPs 149.72.194.74 + 149.72.45.198 blocked), BonOpusSales (Feb 11 2025, 935/32K emails delivered; rest blocked by automated system).
playbook: 1) On '#alert-system spam delivery alert' or Impact alerting indicating Yahoo/AOL blocking IPs, look up the originating account in the spam volume — if >1000 emails in a short window from a single account, suspect compromise. 2) Confirm by checking the email content — if it's crypto/financial scam, treat as a confirmed compromise. 3) Mitigation: disable logins on the offending account, transition fallback to a new sub-user, request IP unblocks from Yahoo, add a temporary hard rate limit. 4) Long-term: more advanced login controls + outbound content scanning (tracked under PL-61115 / SendGrid suspension pattern).

title: RT05/RT06 crash when Datadog agent + app-routine subscriber profiling enabled causes memory/CPU spike
diagnosis: On 2024-07-04 at ~4:30 AM, RT05 and RT06 both crashed within ~30min of each other after the Datadog agent's profiling feature was enabled for the app-routine subscriber. The added profiling overhead caused memory and CPU spikes that exceeded available headroom. No customer impact (just fewer RT api nodes). Mitigation: disabled tracing for the agent; investigation into lowering the sampling rate continues.
playbook: 1) On unexplained RT-node crashes with memory/CPU spikes and no recent deploy, check whether Datadog tracing/profiling was recently enabled on the AppRoutine.Subscriber.Agent. 2) Mitigation: disable DD tracing on that agent. 3) Long-term: lower the DD sampling rate, monitor RT memory baseline, and re-enable in a controlled rollout.

title: DNS resolution failures for *.method.int on Windows fleet — AWS Route53 1024 PPS link-local quota exceeded on DCs

any_of.contains: remote name could not be resolved

match.precedence_note: 2026-06-10: Takes precedence over ki-microservices-method-int-upstream-502-bad-gateway IF any DNS-layer mechanism evidence is present (NXDOMAIN, Name or service not known, remote name could not be resolved, linklocal_allowance_exceeded, ENA pps_allowance_exceeded). Without DNS-layer evidence — even if microservices.method.int hostnames appear in the failing URLs — prefer ki-microservices-method-int-upstream-502-bad-gateway. The 2026-06-04 incident was initially misattributed to this entry because the symptom shape (calls to microservices.method.int failing) matched; the actual layer was HTTP, not DNS.

diagnosis:
Every Windows EC2 instance forwards DNS to two AD domain controllers (prod-dc-01, prod-dc-02), which then forward *.method.int queries to AWS Route53 Resolver at 172.31.0.2. That destination counts against the AWS per-ENI 1024 PPS link-local quota (shared with 169.254.169.253, IMDS, NTP, Windows Licensing). Combined query rate from 11 Windows hosts pushes DCs' link-local PPS over the cap during bursts; AWS silently drops the excess packets at the VPC fabric. DCs' conditional forwarder for method.int had UseRecursion=True, so on forwarder timeout the DC falls back to root-hint recursion. Root hints can't resolve .int (reserved TLD; no public method.int zone), so they return NXDOMAIN, which the DC negatively caches. Windows DNS clients then cache the negative response for 15 minutes (MaxNegativeTtl), extending visible outage well past the actual packet-drop bursts. ENA linklocal_allowance_exceeded confirms shaping events; CloudWatch NetworkPacketsOut on prod-dc-01 doubled (1,557 -> 2,982) at incident time. Affected services: report-generation API, classic API, ms-gateway-api, microservices nodes.

==== HOW TO RECOGNIZE THIS (vs HTTP-layer 502 failures on the same hostname) ====
This KB entry matches ONLY incidents where the DNS layer itself failed. Mandatory mechanism evidence: the alert window must include at least one of (a) `Name or service not known` / `remote name could not be resolved` / `NXDOMAIN` error strings, (b) ENA `linklocal_allowance_exceeded` non-zero on prod-dc-01 or prod-dc-02, or (c) DNS query timeout logs. A 502 Bad Gateway HTTP response with nginx HTML body (`<html>...502 Bad Gateway</html>`) on a `microservices.method.int` URL is NOT this issue — it means DNS resolved, the connection reached the proxy, and the proxy returned 502 because its upstream was unreachable/unhealthy. Match HTTP-layer 502 patterns to `ki-microservices-method-int-upstream-502-bad-gateway` instead.

The error rate signature also differs: this DNS issue produces step-function recovery (sharp drops every 15 minutes as the negative cache expires on each Windows host). An HTTP-layer upstream failure produces sustained steady-state errors for the duration of the upstream's degradation. Use the time-shape to disambiguate when only some of the evidence is present.

NOTE: this can present similarly to ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout (Ocelot timeouts) — both involve calls to microservices.method.int failing. Check the layer-specific evidence before matching either.
playbook:
**Before applying this playbook, verify the mechanism.** Confirm at least one DNS-layer error string is present in the alert window: `Name or service not known`, `remote name could not be resolved`, `NXDOMAIN`, or non-zero ENA `linklocal_allowance_exceeded` on the DCs. A 502 Bad Gateway with nginx HTML body is NOT sufficient — that's an HTTP-layer signal that means DNS already resolved successfully. If only the 502 signature is present, match `ki-microservices-method-int-upstream-502-bad-gateway` instead.

1) Check ENA metrics on Windows DCs (prod-dc-01, prod-dc-02): pps_allowance_exceeded, linklocal_allowance_exceeded. Non-zero in the alert window IS the confirmation. 2) Check Datadog for NetworkPacketsOut spike on DCs (the 2026-05 incident saw a 2x jump 1,557 -> 2,982). 3) Confirm the conditional forwarder on EACH DC points to Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint (rslvr-in-33bec0891b854ea8b at 172.31.223.154 / 172.31.168.212) with UseRecursion=$false. The PIR action items state this was completed on 2026-05-20/21. 4) If the endpoint path drifted/reverted on either DC, that's the root cause — fix the forwarder config on both, then flush DNS clients on affected hosts (`ipconfig /flushdns`) and DCs (`Clear-DnsServerCache`) to clear the 15-minute negative cache. 5) Long-term per PIR: reduce Windows MaxNegativeTtl from 15 minutes to 30 seconds; enable DNS client logging; collect Datadog throttling metrics (bw_*_allowance_exceeded, pps_allowance_exceeded, conntrack_allowance_exceeded, linklocal_allowance_exceeded); add a forwarder-config drift alarm so we know in minutes (not hours) if a DC's conditional forwarder gets reverted again.

title: EDA Orchestrator API 1-minute timeouts on prod-msl-03/04/05 cause Gary-account-only platform slowness (PL-57695)

match.tightening_note: 2026-06-10: require EDA Orchestrator mention in all_of, then require specific 1-minute timeout pattern OR prod-msl host + timeout pattern together. Prevents firing on bare 'timeout' + 'EDA.Orchestrator.Api' which would catch any EDA latency.

diagnosis: The platform experienced intermittent slowness for ~1 hour on 2025-10-06. Datadog metrics + Logstash traced it to the EDA Orchestrator API timing out after a fixed 1 minute, which then delayed upstream runtime-core request processing. EDA Orchestrator is only enabled for the 'Gary accounts' cohort, so only those accounts saw the impact. Root cause was a load-balancing / deployment misconfiguration on prod-msl-03/04/05 — fixed under PL-57695.
playbook: 1) On runtime-core slowness alerts that affect only the Gary-accounts cohort, check the EDA Orchestrator API (eda.methodlocal.int health) for elevated latency / 1-minute timeouts on prod-msl-03/04/05. 2) If timing out, confirm the LB target group includes all three nodes and they all return healthy at the same EDA endpoint. 3) Mitigation: re-balance the EDA Orchestrator deploy across all three nodes (or restart any failing node). 4) PL-57695 was the long-term fix — confirm that LB/deploy config is still correct.

title: Elasticsearch high-disk watermark flips indices read-only → RabbitMQ messages pile up to 40K error-queue cap
diagnosis: Elasticsearch reached its high disk space watermark, ES auto-flipped indices into read-only mode, and writes stopped. With ES rejecting writes, messages piled up in RabbitMQ. Method policy is 40K-message ceiling per queue; once exceeded, messages divert to the error queue. Customers saw intermittent random error messages between 10-11 PM and general slowness throughout the day. Action items: increased the data drive size; the upcoming ES v9 cluster migration is the long-term fix.
playbook: 1) On 'intermittent random error messages' / generalized slowness when no deploy ran, check ES cluster disk usage on each node. If any node is over the high-watermark threshold (default 85%), ES has flipped its indices to read-only. 2) Confirm via RabbitMQ — search for queues at or near the 40K message cap, especially audit-trail or ES-shipper queues. 3) Mitigation: free disk on the affected ES node (close old indices, delete stale snapshots, expand the data volume). 4) Long-term: confirm the ES v9 cluster migration has shipped and the new cluster has appropriate disk headroom / ILM.

title: Field Crew app: empty-state overlay blocks all users when feature flag (auto-create-visit-on-WO) is on for older accounts that don't have the new behavior
diagnosis: A new Field Crew feature that auto-creates a 'visit' when a work order is assigned to a technician was wired behind a release feature flag. The empty-state-overlay dismissal logic was conditioned on the presence of that auto-created visit. For older accounts the feature was not applicable, so no visit existed, the overlay never dismissed, and customers couldn't access Field Crew at all. Two accounts were reported affected. Mitigation: turn the feature flag OFF.
playbook: 1) On 'Field Crew not accessible' / 'empty state overlay' reports, check whether the field-crew feature flag for auto-create-visit-on-WO is on AND the affected account is an older account that does not get visits auto-created. 2) Immediate mitigation: flip the feature flag off for affected accounts (or globally). 3) Permanent fix: change the overlay dismissal condition to check user's actual access to work orders, not the existence of an auto-created visit.

title: Method:Sidebar (Gmail) 'Bandwidth quota exceeded' from Google's auth discovery endpoints
diagnosis: Method:Sidebar (Gmail) users intermittently see 'Bandwidth quota exceeded' on authentication discovery pages and downstream calls. Root cause is Google-side, not Method-side: Google's authentication discovery endpoints throttled during this window, and the same symptom affected other tenants of those endpoints. Google's own issue tracker eventually marked it fixed. Method tests confirmed resolution while some external users still reported residual problems.
playbook: 1) If 'Bandwidth quota exceeded' shows up in Method:Sidebar logs/RUM, this is a Google-side throttle, not Method code. 2) No remediation action on our side. 3) Communicate the workaround/wait pattern: the issue resolves when Google clears the throttle. 4) Optional: check the Google issue tracker for the auth-discovery quota incident referenced in PL-62491 before paging anyone.

title: Diagnostic pattern: 'Unexpected character encountered while parsing value: <' means a backend service received an HTML error page (502/503/504) where it expected JSON — look upstream, not at the deserializer

any_of.contains: Unexpected character encountered while parsing value: <

diagnosis: When you see `Newtonsoft.Json.JsonReaderException: Unexpected character encountered while parsing value: <. Path '', line 0, position 0` in .NET service logs, the calling service is receiving an HTML error page (typically `<html><head><title>502 Bad Gateway</title>...` from nginx, or 503/504 variants) where it expected a JSON response from an HTTP API. Newtonsoft sees the first character `<`, which isn't valid JSON, and immediately throws. The Newtonsoft exception is the SYMPTOM — the ROOT CAUSE is the upstream service or network path returning HTML instead of JSON. Common root causes Method has seen: (1) ki-microservices-method-int-upstream-502-bad-gateway — calls to http://microservices.method.int/* return 502 from nginx because the upstream IIS pool / backend is unreachable. (2) ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota — DNS-layer failure prevents resolution; specifically requires DNS-layer error strings (NXDOMAIN / Name or service not known) to confirm, NOT just the 502 HTML body. (3) IIS app pool recycle on any called service — brief 502 window while the pool warms back up. (4) Load balancer health checks marking nodes unhealthy. (5) Real 5xx from the upstream service. The fact that the failing call was made over HTTP and the response was 'HTML' is the load-bearing evidence; do NOT spend time debugging the Newtonsoft code path itself. Cross-reference: search ES for the exact Url that was called (often present in a sibling `Error.keyword` aggregation field like 'Error Calling Url: http://...'), and identify which upstream service or network hop is returning 502.
playbook: 1) Aggregate ES errors by `Error.keyword` in the incident window (NOT by `Level.keyword` — that just tells you there are errors, not which kind). Look for the SECOND-place error pattern: typically 'Error Calling Url: http://<hostname>/...' with a non-2xx status code. The hostname identifies the failing upstream. 2) **Disambiguate the layer.** Check whether ANY DNS-layer error strings are present in the alert window: `Name or service not known`, `remote name could not be resolved`, `NXDOMAIN`, `linklocal_allowance_exceeded`. If YES → match ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota. If NO → it's an HTTP-layer failure; match ki-microservices-method-int-upstream-502-bad-gateway (for the microservices.method.int hostname specifically) or investigate the upstream HTTP service directly (for other hostnames). 3) Pattern-matching on the symptom shape (calls to microservices.method.int failing) is NOT sufficient evidence for the DNS entry — that's a false-positive mode we hit on 2026-06-04. The DNS PPS quota requires DNS-layer error strings as load-bearing evidence. 4) Count the ratio of Newtonsoft-parse-errors to '502' errors in the window — they should be roughly proportional. If 502s are much higher (10×+), some callers are silently failing without surfacing the deserialize error. 5) When 502s drop, Newtonsoft errors drop with them — they're not independent bugs.
references: Triage report 2026-06-04 — first surfaced when 6,892 AuthService.GetProductFeatureFlag timeouts on PROD-NEW5/6 were correlated to 88 Newtonsoft parse errors + 75 microservices.method.int 502s + 124 MSAuth/MSIdentity 502s. Initially misattributed to ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota — that was wrong; actual layer was HTTP (no DNS-resolver error strings, sustained steady-state error rate not 15-min plateaus). Reattributed to ki-microservices-method-int-upstream-502-bad-gateway after operator review. The misattribution motivated this entry's playbook step 2 (explicit DNS-vs-HTTP layer disambiguation).

title: Cancelled accounts receive payment emails because Intercom sync truncated by FeatureFlagList >255-char overflow (PL-48592)
diagnosis: Customers with cancelled accounts received payment emails from Method that they should not have. Investigation found the emails were sent by Intercom, not Method. Method's Intercom sync was breaking for several accounts because the FeatureFlagList company field exceeded the 255-char max. As a result, cancelled-account states were never synced to Intercom, and Intercom continued to treat cancelled accounts as active for email triggers. Estimated impact: ~125 inactive accounts and ~1,265 active accounts. Hotfix released to address active and inactive accounts during nightly sync; data backfill performed for the 125 inactive. Follow-up observability work in PL-48592.
playbook: 1) On 'cancelled customers receiving emails from Method' complaints, check whether the emails were sent by Method or by Intercom (sender domain in the email). 2) Verify Intercom sync health — search for sync failures linked to FeatureFlagList truncation. 3) If recurrence: hotfix to truncate or chunk FeatureFlagList for Intercom transmission, then backfill stale cancelled-account states. 4) Long-term: confirm PL-48592 observability is in place to detect Intercom-sync drift earlier.

title: iOS 17+ users: keyboard fails to open on customized text-input controls (disabled-state OS behavior change)
diagnosis: iOS 17+ changed how mobile controls respond to being disabled. Method controls that briefly toggle disabled on focus (a customization pattern used by some accounts) now suppress the keyboard. High impact for the few accounts that use this customization on their text inputs. Caught late as a P2 ticket.
playbook: 1) When iOS-mobile users report 'keyboard doesn't open on tap', check the affected account's customization for onFocus disable/enable patterns on text input controls. 2) Confirm iOS version (17+) and that the same screen works for non-customized inputs. 3) Workaround for affected accounts: remove the onFocus disabled toggle from their customization. 4) Long-term per PIR: organizational policy for pro-active testing against major OS updates (championed by John Jones).

title: Wrong version of legacy-syncservice-api deployed breaks QBDT sync + Accounting View Deltas + account signup
diagnosis: On 2026-05-04 multiple symptoms surfaced together: QuickBooks Desktop sync failing, Accounting View Deltas regeneration returning 'Response Not Successful', and new account creation failing (1 signup affected). Root cause: an incorrect (older) build of legacy-syncservice-api was deployed under the belief that it predated certain DevOps code changes; in fact it already contained the problematic code and the newer version had the fix. Once the right build was deployed, QBDT background sync caught up automatically for affected customers.
playbook: 1) If QBDT sync, view-deltas regeneration, and signup are all failing concurrently, suspect a bad legacy-syncservice-api build. 2) Check what version is deployed on the legacy IIS pool host (services.methodlocal.com) vs the last known-good. 3) Mitigation: redeploy the correct (newer) build; background QBDT sync will resume on its own. 4) Long-term per PIR: when a defective version is suspected, the fix forces the project through full regression again before any roll-forward.

title: methodintegration.com domain redirected to GoDaddy parking page from overdue payment → Classic / Report Generation / Tables & Fields down

match.tightening_note: 2026-06-10: required methodintegration.com hostname in all_of and removed bare 'Report Generation' match (too broad — would fire on any Report-Generation-related alert). Mechanism evidence (GoDaddy/parking page/domain-expired language) still must be present in any_of.

diagnosis: Method Classic, Report Generation, and Tables & Fields all suddenly broke. Root cause: the methodintegration.com domain registration payment was overdue on GoDaddy and GoDaddy redirected the domain to their parking page. Action items: Paul purchased the domain for three years, ops@method.me was added as an admin on the GoDaddy account, and the credentials were added to Passbolt.
playbook: 1) On unexplained simultaneous outages of Classic + Report Generation + Tables & Fields with no recent deploy, immediately check whether any Method-owned domain (especially methodintegration.com) has changed DNS / redirects to a registrar parking page. 2) Visit the domain in a browser — if it shows GoDaddy / registrar parking, payment is overdue. 3) Mitigation: pay the domain immediately; DNS will repropagate within minutes-to-hours. 4) Long-term: confirm ops@method.me is on the registrar account, credentials in Passbolt, and renewal is multi-year.

title: MethodTCPIPServer agent stops during deploy of an unrelated web service → QBDT Real-Time Sync down
diagnosis: QBDT Real-Time Sync between Method→QBDT was down for ~45 minutes; the Engine showed as disconnected. Root cause: during a deploy of a web service (NOT MethodTCPIPServer), the MethodTCPIPServer agent stopped operating — even though the deploy did not target it. The deploy should not have affected the agent. Action item is to monitor for recurrence; no permanent fix shipped at PIR time.
playbook: 1) On 'QBDT Real-Time Sync down' alerts shortly after a deploy of any Classic-related web service, check whether the MethodTCPIPServer agent is running on Classic. If not, restart it. 2) Confirm the Engine reconnects. 3) Long-term: instrument for the agent stopping (Centreon or DD agent process check) so this doesn't go undetected.

title: MethodUI outage from sanitization-discrepancy tracking firing excessive ms-analytics calls → SQL pool exhaustion (PL-52451)
diagnosis: A change to track XSS-sanitization discrepancies (compare raw vs sanitized user input) generated excessive and redundant API calls to ms-analytics. Faulty comparison logic flagged minor variations (attribute order, spacing, extra closing tags) as discrepancies; one path compared objects instead of primitives, multiplying call volume. ms-analytics was overwhelmed; SQL Server max-connection-pool hit (~4000 open connections on sql-prod1 vs typical ~1500/server at peak) — taking the whole platform down. Confusion: MethodPheonix surfaced the errors but the actual problem was upstream; recent architecture changes (2 new servers) further delayed root-cause identification. Rollback was delayed by the investigation. Mitigations: batching/deduplication for the discrepancy tracking, fix the comparison logic, expedite rollback decisions when only one service shows symptoms.
